message:
fix(update): registration never initialised COM, and nobody could see it

The second field attempt got through PrepareForSwap, Quiesce and a ten-file Swap,
and died at Register. The log said "register failed: registration failed" and
nothing else.

The reason was being built and thrown away one line from where it was needed.
register_install() stops at the first failure and records which step it was, with
a detail carrying the Win32 code or HRESULT; the wiring exposes that as
lastResult; and the production caller returned only the bool. So a field failure
was indistinguishable from any other. It now logs completed, failedAt and detail.
No state machine types changed -- the requirement was that the HRESULT reach the
log, not that the plumbing be redesigned.

COM was missing from exactly one place: the registration path calls
CoCreateInstance(CLSID_ShellLink) and there is no CoInitialize anywhere in
updater_main, updater_effects or update_registration*. The installer has it in its
own main, and when this code was extracted to be shared the caller's precondition
did not come with it. update_relaunch.cpp already does this correctly -- ask for
an apartment, remember whether this call got it, release only then, and carry on
past RPC_E_CHANGED_MODE because that means somebody else already initialised the
thread. That file is untouched; the fix moves its pattern to the path that lacked
it. createShortcut now returns the HRESULT in a detail, and the destination is
injectable so a test can drive the real shell APIs without writing into every
user's Start menu.

The first attempt's failure turned out to be a different thing: an orphan. The log
recorded "relaunch (required) GNLinkHost.exe: started", which means the host was
already gone -- so what was left was a windowless child whose parent could not be
enumerated, the ownership check could not pass, and it fell through to a direct
request that cannot succeed. With nobody to ask, it is now waited for instead, and
the three failure reasons are three different sentences. Both branches are
asserted: an orphan that leaves lets the swap proceed, and one that never leaves
still abandons -- with a reason that is not "could not ask".

The full sweep caught a defect in that change before it was committed. The first
version treated "parent is not among the targets" as orphaned, but parentPid == 0
means NOT KNOWN, and every caller that describes its targets by hand leaves it
zero -- so all of them were routed into a wait that nothing had asked to stop.
update_effects_test went 210 to 206 and update_release_test 80 to 74. The rule I
broke is the one written in the comment directly above it: 0 means not known, and
a target not known to be owned is asked directly. It now asks whether the parent
has actually exited; unknown and still-alive both mean ask directly, and
ACCESS_DENIED is not a yes.

65 suites, 1838 checks, no failures, on an isolated sweep with nothing else
building -- the two before it overlapped my own target builds and disagreed with
each other, which is a trap this session has already fallen into once. 1820 to
1838 is the new COM suite's 9 plus stop_process going 15 to 24.

Still open: whether GNLinkStream exits on its own when its parent dies. There is
no parent watch and no job object on that path, and if it does not, waiting only
improves the message. Observing it needs the live host stopped, which the tool
permission layer refused, so it is not guessed at here.
